speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, how long have you been experiencing these balance and coordination issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. You mentioned feeling clumsy specifically on the right side; does this ataxia worsen when you walk in the dark, and have you noticed any slurred speech or difficulty swallowing recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a significant detail; given your history of Crohn's disease and recent use of natalizumab, we must urgently assess for PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy). Have you noticed any new visual disturbances, headaches, or worsening weakness in your limbs since starting this medication?

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

Given your significant immunosuppression from Crohn's and natalizumab use, combined with unilateral limb ataxia, I have already requested an MRI Brain with contrast to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions. I will review those images immediately to finalize the assessment.
